scoring_justification: Transition temperature can be recomputed from the susceptibility curve in mc_observables.csv; phase diagram points and tricritical point are directly compared to the paper's MC gold values within defined tolerances.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference transition temperature, phase diagram line, tricritical point
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper’s MC results: Tc=1.690 at D=0, tricritical point D/J=-1.974, T/J=0.56, and linear phase-diagram interpolation from end-points (Fig. 5).
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from the paper text and figure; phase diagram approximated by linear fit between the two known extreme points.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper’s self-reported MC values, not invented.

schema.description: All quantities are in natural units (J=1, kB=1).

outputs.description: Temperature-dependent observables (magnetization, susceptibility, specific heat, Binder cumulant) for the Blume-Capel model at D/J=0, h/J=0. The checker will verify that the curves are physically plausible and that the transition temperature extracted from them meets the paper's value within a tolerance.
Critical temperature Tc/J as a function of crystal field D/J for h/J=0. The checker will compare selected Tc values against reference data within a tolerance.
The tricritical point coordinates extracted from the phase diagram. The checker will compare these values to the paper's reported values within a tolerance.

output_contract.notes: All outputs are produced by Monte Carlo simulation only; the introduced effective-field approximation (IEFT) is not part of the reproduction task. The checker uses hidden gold values from the paper's MC results and applies threshold_or_better scoring: meeting or exceeding the reference earns full credit.

steps.description: Extract Tc from susceptibility peak in mc_observables.csv and compare to paper MC value 1.690 ± 0.02
Compare Tc values at selected D/J points to expected linear phase diagram within 0.05
Compare tricritical point coordinates to paper values within 0.02
